compose: This server's container belongs to Docker Compose: only its name, its public address and its cross-server switches are edited here.
flag.bridgeIn: Its chat goes into the cross-server bridge
flag.none: This game can reach no players from the dashboard: no cross-server switches.
flag.steamListing: Listed in the Steam server browser
hint.bindAddress: Host address the game ports are published on. 0.0.0.0: every interface. 127.0.0.1: this host only (players cannot reach it directly). Or one address of this host.
hint.publicHost: Address players connect to (host name or IP, no port), shown on the fleet, the server's page and the join page. Empty: the address under Settings → Network.
hint.steamList.pz: Steam's server list: Project Zomboid registers with Steam and is queried on UDP 16261. Forward 16261 and 16262 (UDP) from the router and keep “Listed in the Steam server browser” on, otherwise it does not appear — players can still join directly with the address.
hint.steamList.valheim: Steam's server list: Valheim answers on the query port (game port + 1, UDP). Forward the game port and the query port from the router and keep “Listed publicly” on in the configuration — off, the server answers no queries at all. Players can still join directly with the address and the port.
off.body: Switching off stops the container and takes the server out of every job (watchdog, backups, restarts, announcements). Its data stays.
off.confirmBody: The container is stopped now; players are disconnected.
off.failed: The server could not be switched off.
off.setupLink: Switch it on again on its page.
off.title: Switch off
problem.bindAddress: The bind address must be an IP address (for example 0.0.0.0 or 127.0.0.1), not a host name.
problem.image: Image and image tag are required.
problem.port: Every port must be a number between 1 and 65535.
problem.publicHost: The public address is a host name or IP address, without spaces or slashes.
problem.resources: Memory limit and heap must be whole numbers, CPU cores a number.
recreate.confirmOff: The stopped container is replaced by a new one with these values.
recreate.confirmOn: The server is stopped, backed up and started again with the new container. Players are disconnected.
recreate.failed: Saved, but the container could not be recreated.
recreate.noteOff: These changes need a new container. Saving replaces the stopped container; nothing is started.
recreate.noteOn: These changes need a new container. Saving recreates it: a backup first, then the new container, then a boot check; if the server does not come up, the old one is restored.
remove.body: Removes the container and the server from the dashboard, with its statistics, schedules and stored password. The audit log stays. This cannot be undone.
remove.delete: Delete the data in {{path}} as well — the world is gone for good
remove.doneKept: {{key}} was removed; its data is still on disk.
remove.failed: The server could not be removed.
remove.keep: Keep the data in {{path}} (a new server with the same data directory finds the world again)
remove.switchOffFirst: Only a switched-off server can be removed. Switch it off first.
remove.title: Remove server
saveFailed: The changes could not be saved.
